text: 58-year-old female. The patient has been treated for community-acquired pneumonia with levofloxacin on the medical floor. She reports developing watery diarrhea with at least 9 episodes within the last two days, accompanied by lower abdominal discomfort and cramping.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your recent levofloxacin use, I need to check for *Clostridioides difficile* infection. REQUEST TEST: Stool toxin EIA and GDH antigen. Do you have any history of recurrent abdominal issues or recent hospitalizations prior to this pneumonia?

text: It is surprising that the PCR test came back normal despite the clinical presentation and leukocytosis. speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical picture of watery diarrhea and leukocytosis following levofloxacin use is highly suggestive of *C. difficile* infection, despite the negative PCR, which can occasionally yield false negatives or reflect a toxin-negative, PCR-positive strain variant.
